title: Release, Observe and Recover
concept: Keep a known-good version until the candidate is healthy

writing.summary: Keep a known-good version until the candidate is healthy.
writing.rule: A failed readiness check preserves the previous active version.
writing.explanation:
Delivery continues after uploading bytes. A candidate can build successfully and fail a migration or readiness check in the target environment. Retain the previous active version while preparing the candidate, promote only after the required health evidence, and preserve a concrete recovery path.

The state transition in this lab receives the current version, candidate and readiness observations. Reject a blank candidate, an unchanged version or a candidate without successful required checks. On every rejection return the original active version; a partially configured candidate is not an active release. A real database migration may be irreversible, so reverting an executable is not automatically a schema rollback. Prefer compatible expand/contract changes and test recovery against actual persistent state. The capstone asks for an incident record showing the failing condition, observed data and successful recovery rather than a screenshot of a green pipeline.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run the capstone acceptance checks, introduce a failed readiness condition, retain the old version, and document the recovery.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises keep a known-good version until the candidate is healthy. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Return candidate,true only for a nonblank changed candidate with checks_ok and ready both true. Every refused promotion returns current,false unchanged. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: A candidate fails readiness. Which version remains active?
answers: The failed candidate because it uploaded successfully
No version; delete the previous artifact first
writing.feedback: Upload or build success is insufficient to replace an active service.

recall.question: Why does `promote("v1", "v1", true, true)` return `("v1", false)` even though checks and readiness passed?
recall.answer: An unchanged version is not a promotion, just like a blank candidate or a failed check. Every rejection returns the original active version with `false`, so a partially configured candidate never becomes the active release.

recall.question: The new executable ran a database migration and then failed readiness. Why might switching back to the old executable not fully recover?
recall.answer: Reverting an executable is not a schema rollback, and a migration may be irreversible, so the old version may not work with the changed data. Prefer compatible expand/contract migrations and test recovery against real persistent state.
